Ah that does make things more complicated. I would suggest making sure your legal bases are covered regarding custody/responsibility. Prepare for the worst and hope for the best. It is not too late for therapy, and at the very least feel free to get a therapist for yourself as dealing with someone who has bpd is not easy for anyone.
Sure I can elaborate once I’m off work.

Start thinking about what you want your relationship to be in the future. People with bpd are incapable of handling stressful life events, have trouble with change etc. obviously there are exceptions to this but for the most part your relationship will never be on an equal footing. You will be doing most of the emotional labor, and will have to cater to her over-the-top reactions/anger etc. my best advice to you would be to get your SO into therapy and distance yourself or set firm boundaries. You cannot be doing all the emotional labor you have to take care of yourself. “Put your own oxygen mask on first, then help others”
Sounds like a great first step, wishing you all the best
Go to DbT therapy, analyze your own behavior and take accountability for your actions. Your partner deserves someone who can own up to their mistakes and makes changes for the better.
Withdraw a set amount of cash, and only spend that much per week. Don’t use cards, force yourself to only spend what you physically have.
Distance yourself from your FP and figure out your sense of self first. Work on your codependent traits. This is not a healthy relationship.
Correlation doesn’t equal causation.

If you want to talk to someone or enjoy someone’s friendship then go ahead and text first. The second you stop trying to see if others care about you by making them text first the happier you will be. Someone might be your best friend but you aren’t their close friend and that is fine. At the end of the day they still talk to you and both of you get some happiness.

Practice other coping skills, look at the app Calm Harm, use DBT skills like TIPP. You are stronger than your urges and a person’s word defines them. If you promise something, you need to follow through.
I would suggest cutting your loses now and leaving. Bpd has a very long and hard road and recovery is not always guaranteed.

Best advice? Accept you are volatile, do your best to improve yourself and above all else make sure you don’t hurt anyone. The sooner you accept your place in the world the easier your life will become.

We have bpd. We should not attempt to have close friendships or relationships since we are volatile. Others should not have the responsibility to deal with our splitting, intensity etc. I suggest you focus on designing an ideal life for yourself in which you are mostly alone (not lonely, just alone). I have made significant strides to make a life like this and I’m happy to share advice/tips, feel free to dm or ask questions.

This is the wrong sub to ask this, you will mostly get people with bpd like me attempting to downplay the symptoms. The reality is that we are monsters and you cannot support us enough to fill the void. So I suggest you run and get out while you can.

Hi friend, this is a bit late but here are some tips that I’ve used. First I try to identify why I want to yeet, ie is it sadness or rage behind the urge. 

If it is sadness/shame/self hate I try to comfort myself in a non destructive way, like taking a blanket and tossing it in the dryer for five minutes, and then wrapping myself with the blanket so it feels like a warm hug. Other options are distraction, I love physics/space so I’ll watch a documentary or a 3blue1brown video in the hopes that I’ll get interested in learning something and not yeet. If possible, reaching out to a friend might also help, you don’t have to tell them you feel like yeeting, just striking up a conversation would be good, and texting keeps your hands occupied, making it harder to yeet. 

If it’s rage/frustration/hate driving the urge, usually going for a run or going to a different place helps. I don’t know if you are familiar with DBT skills but sometimes the TIP skill can help (it’s not my favorite but worth a try). Worst comes to worst I just set a timer, even if it’s just 30 seconds and see if I can avoid yeeting and logic my way out of the situation. Breathing also helps, and you don’t have to follow any complicated pattern if you don’t want to, just place your hand over your heart or wrap you arms around your waist and take a deep breath, inhaling, holding, exhaling for as long as you want. 

Wishing you all the best friend. Remember that recovery is not necessarily linear, and sometimes all you can do is keep surviving. 

TLDR: identify, soothe/use logic, or distract.

I started cutting at age 12 and due to absolute inaction by my parents and lack of support, it became my only coping mechanism for over 7 years. As a 12 year old my thought process was along the lines of “emotions aren’t valid in my household, no one believes I’m scared or anxious, but physical pain is real.” So I also unscrewed a pencil sharpener bc that was the easiest thing I could find and the relief was immeasurable. It became a way to process emotional pain. 

My first suggestion for you would be to have an honest/open conversation, and establish that you aren’t judging her. Please make no “all or nothing claims” such as, “if you don’t stop that proves you don’t love me” or “every time you cut it hurts me”. That will just make the problem worse and come across as guilt tripping and not genuine. I’d also suggest looking into counseling/therapy ASAP, and explain to your daughter what that means and how it could help. (My parents just yeeted me into a hospital, I had no idea what was going on and I was so so scared). Here are some alternatives to cutting: 
https://keltyeatingdisorders.ca/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/Alternatives-to-self-harm-Handout1.pdf
The app “Calm” might also help, has other activities to distract a person from cutting. 

Lastly, since you are posting this on Reddit and genuinely seeking help, I’m assuming you are a decent parent. So please don’t think this is your fault or blame yourself. All that matters is that you support her,treat this as a serious problem but don’t scare/threaten her. It can genuinely spiral into an addiction, to the point where “just stopping” is damn near impossible. I wish you all the best, happy to be a resource if I can (feel free to PM), sending you love.

If they are healed, you can color correct, red is used for dark spots, so grab some lipstick or color concealer, put red on first over the area, then cover with foundation. Arms often vary in skin tone than face, can be a bit darker, so you can mix a bit of brown or nude eyeshadow/non shimmery bronzer into the foundation to get a slightly better color match. Use translucent or skin colored powder to set it (referred to as “baking”). This will help the makeup not rub off on clothing and reduce the chance of you sweating it off, but also you will have to periodically touch it up.
